publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE/IAS Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The need for regenerated voltage control of an AC variable speed drive occurs when a mechanical system connected to an induction motor causes the motor to rotate at a higher frequency than the control frequency of the variable speed providing power to the motor. This paper reviews resistive and line regeneration options for control of regenerated energy of fixed bus PWM drives.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Voltage sag mitigation through ridethrough coordination
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE/IAS Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The voltage sags/dips impact on industrial processes can be mitigated using ridethrough coordination. The utility predicted for the new plant site: the depth, duration and number of expected sags; and the number of expected outages. The predictions were provided so they could be included in the new machinery quotations. Because the ridethrough predictions for the machinery at the new plant site were known up front and site specific, mitigating the effects of voltage sag could be built into the machinery and did not necessarily require UPS type equipment. Management weighed additional purchase cost with long term downtime cost based on the machine vs. utility specifications and selected the best economic alternative.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Are you certain you understand the economics for applying ASD systems to centrifugal loads?
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE/IAS Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The advantages gained by using AC adjustable-speed drives (ASDs) on HVAC fans, pumps, compressors and other equipment have been widely publicized and their use in industry has been on a steady increase. Details presented include a layman's guide to fan laws, calculation of potential savings based on the three choices of variable air volume control, and evaluation of claims made by vendors. All dollar values presented are approximate, and are based on 1994 energy and equipment costs in the Southeast. Brand names are included to present a cross-section of equipment available and the listing is not intended to be all inclusive.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Decision surface modeling of textile spinning operations using neural network technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE/IAS Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The authors study the spinning operations in textile manufacturing. An attempt to "metamodel" the relation between key inputs and performance measures using neural network technology is reported. Two different neural network models, namely a backpropagation neural network and a fuzzy control neural network, were investigated. According to their experience, both models are capable of providing high quality predictions. In addition, results obtained using a fuzzy controller for the learning rate suggest a significant potential for speeding up the training process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real-time system for data acquisition and control of batch dyeing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE/IAS Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: A real-time system has been developed for the monitoring and control of batch dyeing processes. The system, though developed for batch dyeing, is a generic data acquisition and control tool compliant with POSIX (IEEE 1003.4) and other standards. The system allows for the rapid prototyping of general real-time data acquisition and control systems, while supporting a rich set of development tools to enable networking, window-based applications programming, and object-oriented programming. Currently, the system combines a real-time multitasking operating system with full TCP/IP networking support. Using a VMEbus backplane, the system can also support multiple CPUs and full bus arbitration. Various drivers have been written to enable A/D, D/A, DIG, GPIB, SCSI, as well as serial and parallel communication (RS232).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE/IAS Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The National Electrical Code requires the protection of each motor circuit by a short circuit protective device, that is, a set of fuses or a circuit breaker. Under certain conditions however, the NEC permits more than one motor or load to be protected by the same short circuit protective device. This is called "group motor installation" or "group fusing". Group fusing has taken on a new meaning and respectability with the introduction of starters equipped with built-in magnetic trip units. These starters are called IEC manual starters. The application, the advantages, and the limitations of group installation is examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Applying current limiting fuses with modern molded case circuit breakers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE/IAS Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The application of current limiting fuses to reduce short circuit duty is complicated by the current limiting aspects of modern breaker design. The problem of applying current limiting fuses in conjunction with modern design breakers is explored in a new installation. This installation is a 3000 kVA unit substation in a cogeneration facility. This paper analyzes a problem encountered in a design where modern breakers were installed downstream of current limiting fuses and extrapolates the findings to other applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power reliability study and improvement in a South American fiber plant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE/IAS Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The current international business climate is creating opportunity for technical cooperation between partners having diverse resources and experience. Synthetic fiber production and quality is significantly affected by power system reliability, which is poor in many underdeveloped nations. Some "lessons learned" in the USA were applied to a Venezuelan location through a systematic study of the facility, parameter measurement, and review of improvement options. A static inverter and high inertia motor alternator set having 30-second ride-through capability were found to be justified and-effective in this situation. The study approach is presented along with findings, improvement options, and implementation methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Utilizing serial communications in control systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE/IAS Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: An application utilizing a serial communications data highway to interface control system components is reviewed. In this application, variable speed drives are integrated into the control system by connecting them to a PLC remote I/O data highway.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design elements of the modern spinning control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1994 IEEE/IAS Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The production of synthetic fibers in today's market demands that the production process be flexible, quick to respond, reliable, configurable and measurable. This paper discusses how important process control attributes may be managed through the use of an integrated control system. Also, the paper discusses the formation of a spinning control system that uses single motor drives (usually synchronous motors) and programmable controllers. The issues and advantages are presented from the fiber manufacturer's perspective.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
